Closes #277.

title: Add pre/post deploy hooks
description:
A number of RStudio Connect customers have struggled with getting push-button deployment working because the HTTP defaults in the package don't work in their environment. This is significantly exacerbated by the fact that RStudio does push-button deployments with `--vanilla` R sessions, so it's not possible to inject R code that runs inside the deployment process using the usual `.Rprofile`/`Rprofile.site` mechanisms. 

This change makes deployment more customizable for these advanced cases by adding two mechanisms:

1. An rsconnect-specific set of startup scripts. These allow customers to set rsconnect options to be used for deployment at the site, user, or project level. 

2. A pair of user-defined options which provide functions to be called prior to (and after) deployment. 

Using these tools, it is possible to do arbitrarily complex pre-flight checks and post-deploy cleanup. Ideally most customers won't have to use them, but for those with difficult authentication configurations, it'll provide a useful escape hatch.  

Closes #283.

title: Add function to forget deployments
description:
This change makes it possible to remove locally cached deployment information for an application.

Closes #267.

title: provide way to write publish record in site directory when publishing website via deployApp
description:
If you publish a website (the rendered files) via `rsconnect::deploySite`, it creates the publish record (rsconnect folder) in the website project folder, not in the _site (build output) folder.

However, the IDE uses rsconnect::deployApp for all types of deployments, including websites, and this was resulting in the folder being created under the _site folder where it is: (1) prone to being deleted when blowing away _site and rebuilding the site and (2) not found by the IDE when looking for previous publishes.

Added a new optional parameter to deployApp which allows customizing the location of the rsconnect publish record. Alternative was to have IDE start using deploySite, but that had other consequences and would have also required changes to this package.

title: Ask RSC for Title Updates
description:
This PR introduces a change to `rsconnect::deployments` to account for the fact that in RSC 1.6.8 and above the title can be changed on the Connect end.

This change to `rsconnect` will cause the IDE's publish dialogs to pick up title changes from RSC _each time the content source file is opened_ or _any time content is published_. 

Validated against shinyapps.io to ensure nothing broke.

Also validated the case where the deployment record (rsconnect) folder is deleted, and the case where RSC doesn't respond successfully with the title name (e.g. if the content has been deleted or the publisher's permissions have been changed to viewer).

Small validation note: 

The title change on RSC will not be picked up by the IDE if the source file is left open and the user repeatedly: selects the publish drop down, changes the title on RSC,  reselects the publish drop down _all without ever publishing_.

title: write publish record to website root when publishing rendered files
description:
This is in support of fixes here: https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/pull/3409

When publishing the rendered files for a website, write the rsconnect folder (publish record) to the website root instead of putting it in the _site folder where it is (1) prone to being deleted when rebuilding the site and (2) not found by the IDE when looking for previous publishes.

title: default to curl + bump timeout for Windows
description:
NOTE: We probably don't want to merge this right away since there is almost surely some larger discussion required as to whether we can just flip the switch and move from RCurl to curl (especially regarding certificates and other authentication issues)

---

The version of OpenSSL bundled by RCurl on Windows (at the time of this commit) was 1.0.0o, which is too old. The 'curl' package bundles an up-to-date version of curl and OpenSSL, so its usage should be preferred.

Closes #286.

title: Update cookie regular expression to be closer to spec
description:
Connected to #229

Old way: 

- `"^(\\w+)\\s*=\\s*([^;]*)(;|$)"` means "start of line followed by a group of word characters, followed by any number of spaces, followed by an equal sign, followed by any number of spaces, followed by any number of characters not a semicolon, followed by a semicolon or EOL"

New way:

- `"^([^;=, ]+)\\s*=\\s*([^;,]*)(;|$)"` means "start of line followed by **a group of characters not semicolon, equals sign, comma, or space**, followed by (unmodified from the old way...)"

Tests added to cover the offending cases.

title: Update built-in certs; use them when no system store exists
description:
This change fixes #220 on Windows. 

In #212, we stopped stomping on the system SSL cert store; instead, we locate it, and append just the certificates we need. 

It turns out however that on some Windows configurations there isn't a system cert store anywhere on the search path, which leaves us with an incomplete store. To address this, we now use our built-in cert store if none of the known SSL cert store paths exist.

This change also updates the built-in cert store (it was about 5 years old).

title: Use hash of public key instead of random token

This change fixes the issue described in #221: instead of using `sample()` to generate a random, unique token, we hash the public key (a large, random value derived from a separate random stream) to generate a token ID. 

Note that this change results in roughly a doubling of the token ID length. As users don't have to type or generally even see these URLs, this is probably fine, but we could discard some of the hashed bytes if it becomes an issue.

title: Improve SSL certificate support; closes #178
description:
This change greatly improves support for SSL certificates in the rsconnect package. 

Organizations who use self-signed certificates have a lot of trouble getting them to work with the package; see #178 and #148 for examples. The primary source of the pain is that we currently ship our *own* CA bundle, to ensure that users can always publish to shinyapps.io even if the required root CA certificate is not present in their system certificate store. Prior to this change, the only way to change the CA bundle used was to replace this file in the package installation, which had to be done for every user, and re-done every time the package was upgraded.

The change adds the following tools for working with certificates:

### Global options

The new `rsconnect.ca.bundle` option makes it possible to specify your own CA bundle. This option can also be supplied in an environment variable, `RSCONNECT_CA_BUNDLE`. 

It is now also possible to globally suppress SSL certificate validation in the package by setting the new `rsconnect.check.certificate` option to `FALSE`. This is obviously ill-advised and insecure, but provides an escape hatch that will allow deployments to work even if the correct SSL configuration cannot be achieved.

### Per-server options

You can now specify a certificate to *append* to the default CA bundle when working with a particular server, using the `certificate` argument to `addServer()`. 

This makes it possible for end users to supply certificates, without touching global options, permissions, or external files (the certificate is stored along with the server information in the configuration directory). We hope to update the RStudio IDE to make it possible to attach a certificate when adding a Connect account.

title: Add more verbose logging with timestamps
Add support for collaborative deployment
description:
This change adds support for collaborative deployment (that is, deploying content to another user's account) to the rsconnect package.

There are two major changes which make this possible:

### Publisher: storing host URL and server username

When publishing content, we now write out two additional fields to the deployment record: the raw host URL and raw server username. Previously, the deployment record contained only the local nicknames for these values, which made it impossible to determine the account that owned the content on machines other than the one that deployed the content.

### Collaborator: publish specific app ID

If you're updating someone else's application, there are two different accounts in play: the account you're deploying *from* (which presumably you already have registered) and the account you're deploying *to*.

To spare users the pain of trying to specify two different accounts when deploying, we've just added a single, optional parameter to deployApp: `appId`. When present, this will try to deploy to the given appId (regardless of who owns it). 

There's an accompanying change on the IDE side which allows you to see both the source and destination accounts. It engages only when you're updating someone else's application, and looks like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/470418/28291795-d914ff18-6b00-11e7-94aa-274e5174e264.png)

title: Add session-long support for cookies
description:
Enables all three HTTP modes in rsconnect to support cookies. This is important for RSC in HA environments where the load balancer will set a cookie to ensure session stickiness.

Largely based off of [this RFC](http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2109.txt). Intentional deviations or omissions from the RFC are called out in the code (e.g. the inclusion of the port in the hostname for domains, no support for the `domain` field on cookies). 

Happy to take input on the R code or if there are cleaner ways to implement portions of this. Also hoping to get eyes on the changes around `http.R:220`. I'm using an explicit equality check here in order to be case-insensitive, but that means leaving behind `identical` which makes us vulnerable to `NULL` comparisons. title: permit fallback to CRAN during snapshot
description:
This PR relaxes the requirement that packages installed from sources will cause a Packrat snapshot to fail. Now, if a user attempts to deploy an application that makes use of a package installed from sources, Packrat will accept the snapshot, and warn the user that Packrat will attempt to restore that package from CRAN for future restores.

Note that the restore behavior can still be overridden based on active Packrat options (e.g. `external.packages` or `ignored.packages`), so the primary effect here is just to ensure that snapshots that users make with packages installed from sources succeed; it's still possible that attempts to deploy / run their application could fail if the user has not synchronized their under-development package with their local CRAN-like repository (or whatever mechanism they're using to get packages installed on the Connect side).

If this PR is taken, it should likely be taken in tandem with a bump in the Packrat version: https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/commit/d4b591e11f2e43b4b18ba8ef48635f5f6f809805

Improve deploying from a packrat project
description:
This PR aims to improve two use cases:

1. When rsconnect is deploying from a packrat project.
The existing packrat lock file is respected (instead of generating a new one). 

2. When using the RSC API to deploy content pulled from a remote repo
One use case for the RSC API is for Jenkins (or another CI tool) to deploy content to Connect from a remote repository. In this case, rsconnect is not being called from the development environment. The packrat lock file describing the original environment needs to be respected. This packrat lock file can come from a user developing in a packrat project, or from a user running: `packrat::.snapshotImpl(snapshot.sources=FALSE)` prior to committing to the repo.

This PR also checks to see if a .Rprofile is being added that contains `source("packrat/init.R")` and comments out that line if it exists. This is useful because a) packrat shouldn't be initiated on the target server and b) packrat is always ignored by default when adding files to the bundle - this means the default behavior when deploying from a packrat project is to include the .Rprofile but exclude packrat which causes an error

title: ignore knitr cache when determining bundle files
Improve diagnostic output during deployment
description:
This change addresses feedback from the support team concerning error attribution in deployment failures. Deployment is a complex process involving many parts (including Packrat for bundling, lots of logic in the rsconnect package itself, and then unbundling/rendering on the server end), and when a failure occurs it's not clear exactly where it's coming from. 

Towards that end, this change bundles a number of improvements:

There is now a **verbose output mode** for deployment. In this mode, the log is annotated with extra information, including the `deployApp` call and R session information, and most tracing options are enabled for the duration of the deployment, including those that log more detailed HTTP errors, and the JSON communication between the client and server.  Note that this part of the change changes function signatures. 

There is a **new option**, `rsconnect.error.trace`. This option, when enabled, installs a custom error handler that prints stack traces when a local error occurs during deployment.  It's designed mostly to be used by the above switch, but can also be used standalone. 

Errors from **Packrat** are now explicitly marked as such, even in non-verbose mode. 

There is a planned IDE side of this change: We'll add an affordance to the IDE, probably in the publish preferences pane, to make it possible for customers (and developers) to turn on the verbose output mode for deployments originating from the IDE so they can share the diagnostic logs with the support team when that's necessary (hopefully rarely).

title: Increase max bundle size, and add file count throttle
description:
Currently, the maximum bundle size has two conflated responsibilities:

1) Prevent the intentional deployment of bundles that are too large for the server to accept. 

2) Prevent the accidental deployment of enormous directories (which will take a very long time to bundle) by bailing out early while counting the files in the directory.

However, the max bundle size is currently set at 1GB, which is too low for some shinyapps accounts. Therefore this change attempts to separate the concerns a little, by doing the following:

1) Increasing the deployment cap to 3GB, the highest currently supported bundle size

2) Improving the UX when deploying oversized directories by capping the number of files at 10,000 -- this is fast enough to terminate enumeration in a reasonable time

Note that after this change we will be perfectly willing to publish e.g. a 2GB bundle to a basic shinyapps.io account, where it will be summarily rejected by the server. I think that it's okay to let the server be ultimately responsible for enforcing max bundle sizes as otherwise we'll have to keep the package in sync with rules that could vary from server to server (and with time as we adjust thresholds on our hosted products), or introduce additional complexity to read and apply the rules from the server.

If it is useful, I will gladly try to replace RJSONIO/RCurl with `jsonlite/curl` as well.

title: Add support for Connect application title
description:
This change makes it possible to supply a freeform, descriptive title when deploying an application. 

```
deployApp(appName = "clandestine", appTitle="My Spying Notes!", ...)
```

When deploying a new application, it is possible to omit `appName` entirely and just supply an `appTitle`. In this case a suitable name will be generated automatically, or an error will be raised if one cannot be inferred. This mechanism is also exposed (via `generateAppName`) so that front ends (i.e. RStudio) can use identical logic.

The application's title is persisted as part of its local deployment record, and returned in `rsconnect::deployments()`. 

Note that the title is ignored, without a warning, on services that do not support it, such as shinyapps.io. In this case, the title is still stored locally as a convenient descriptor.

title: Improve and expose app bundle generator
description:
Today there are two parallel implementations of the Shiny app bundle generator -- that is, the function that returns the list of files that should be bundled, given a directory. There's one in the IDE and one here in the **rsconnect** package. They do roughly the same thing but have slightly different features; for instance, the one in the IDE halts recursion after reaching a size cap, but ignores all dotfiles, whereas the one in this package has an unbounded size but has a more specific list of dotfiles it ignores. 

This has generated some confusion, so this change merges the behaviors and moves the unified function to the package (a later change to the ID will invoke the package function to generate the bundle file list).

The net change (from the package perspective) is:
1. There is a new option, `rsconnect.max.bundle.size`. If an attempt is made to deploy a bundle exceeding this size, an error is generated.
2. A new function is exposed which generates the bundle file list. This can be used by a front end (i.e. the IDE) to generate the file list.

title: Implement deploySite function
description:
This PR makes use of the [`site_generator`](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/pull/653) work in **rmarkdown** to implement a high-level `deploySite` function. A couple of assumptions regarding how RSC will handle these sites on the server are baked in here so we should discuss and then revise as appropriate. 

We now deploy with `contentCategory = "site"` (and this is not customizable by design so that RSC can trigger different logic for this category of content). We had previously gone in the direction of `contentCategory = "book"` then simply treating it as a "Document" in the UI. For the time being we can allow "site" to default into the "Documents" category as "book" did however I'd propose that we eventually create a new category named "Websites" which will include books, blogs, sites generated automatically from data analysis projects, etc. 

We now have a `sourceCode = FALSE` parameter that indicates whether this is a static publish or a publish with source code. Static publish works today without any changes to RSC, however source code publish will need something like the following:
1. If a new bundle is deployed with `contentCategory = "site"` and `sourceCode = TRUE` then call the `rmarkdown::site_generator` function in order to build the site and ascertain what directory it's output should be served from (e.g. '.', '_site', or '_book')
2. Serve requests to the deployed application from the output directory (e.g. _book) rather than the root.
3. Realize that this is a class of "report" that cannot be attached to an email and behave accordingly when sending out emails.

Paramaterized websites are not yet addressed (and will take some work in a number of packages to get right so I'd suggest we add this later if there is demand for it).

title: retain global deployment history
description:
We now record all deployments in a centralized deployments/history.dcf file. This is done so that front ends can show a view of all recent / previously published content.

Note that we record the data in a single file that is arranged in reverse chronological order (this is so that a front end interested in e.g. only the last 30 deployments could read that far and stop).

There is no limit to the size of the file but note that 4 deployments take about 1K of space so a 1MB file would cover ~ 4000 deployments.

title: Show more detailed HTTP error information
description:

title: Add support for publishing single-file Shiny applications
description:
This change makes it possible to deploy single-file Shiny applications to RStudio Connect.

These applications fall somewhere in between R Markdown documents and Shiny applications in structure:
- Like R Markdown documents, deployment records for single-file applications are specific to the file rather than the directory, so it is possible to have several single-file Shiny applications in one directory, each with their own deployment records.
- Like Shiny applications, single-file applications are bundled with their entire directory by default; unlike R Markdown documents, we don't generally believe we can accurately infer their dependencies.

To deploy a single-file Shiny application, all that is necessary is to pass the name of the .R file containing the application as the `appPrimaryDoc`. When the application is bundled, this `.R` file will be renamed to `app.R` in the bundle, so no changes to Connect are necessary (Shiny will run the directory without additional changes).

Note that there's an upcoming change to Shiny (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/commit/85e2e00bc4914f7670f87ed285f51b9344ff7289) which will allow us to make a more elegant change once it's on CRAN and we feel comfortable requiring it. After the change, Shiny's `runApp` accepts a `.R` file as a parameter, so it won't be necessary to rename to `app.R`, instead, we'll just bundle the app as-is and indicate the `.R` file in the bundle metadata, and make a change to Connect to invoke `runApp` on the file specified in the metadata.

title: Make server URL validation more robust
description:
This change addresses some ongoing confusion about whether to use http or https in the IDE's server URL textbox, and how to specify it if so, by accepting a wider variety of inputs and trying URL variations with short timeouts so that even some incorrectly specified URLs can be used. The two major changes are:
- It is no longer necessary to specify http or https on the URL. If you do specify it, we'll try the protocol you named first, but also try the other one if it fails.
- If the server returns a redirect on the URL, we'll try again at the redirected URL. 

Once this is in, the IDE will lose the http/https checkbox, and let the user just type the server URL freehand (with a cue suggesting the right format).

title: Use packrat to generate shinyapps.io manifests
description:
Previously content being deployed to connect used `packrat` to detect dependencies whiling still generating the manifest from code within the `rsconnect` package.  The goal of this PR is to generate the manifest using the same `packrat` snapshot that connect uses. This eliminates the need for the old dependency detection code. This also has the benefit of allowing content deployed to shinyapps.io to understand dependencies detected by `packrat` including 3rd-party CRAN-like repositories and other sources in the future.

NOTE: There is shinyapps.io server side changes that must be deployed for this to work so don't merge without checking with me.

description:
An "orphaned" deployment record is one for which no account is registered, e.g.

Now there's a deployment record for `~/foo`, but it cannot be used to update the application because the `bob` account has been removed. For most purposes we want to ignore orphaned records, so this is now the default; it's still possible to get the previous behavior by passing `excludeOrphaned = FALSE`.

If, during this 100ms interval, content was emitted to _both_ streams, the output may not appear in the order it was emitted. 

We have a bug on the RStudio side to fix this but it's likely going to be nontrivial; in the meantime, this small change ensures that the failure line is always the last one emitted.

title: Don't post-process gathered content from HTTP responses with RCurl
description:
This change fixes a bug in which RSConnect can mangle returned JSON. 

RCurl's `basicTextGatherer`, with default settings, attempts to decode Unicode escape sequences of the form `\u0000`. Unfortunately, it also has a side effect: it turns sequences of two backslashes into one backslash, but leaves sequences of one backslash alone. This means that backslashes that were formerly escaped become meaningful, and if they are in an unlucky location (such as next to a quote), they will make the entire text unparseable.

Since there's no known need to decode Unicode escape sequences here, the fix is just to turn off this RCurl feature for our usage. 

(I've also de-duped `handleResponse` since there's no need for separate connect/lucid copies of this function.)

title: Add support for publishing single files via deployDoc
description:
This change adds support for publishing single files via `deployDoc`. Formerly, a single file had to be HTML for this to work. 

N.B.: Because it doesn't specifically name PDFs, this dramatically loosens the restrictions on what we're willing to publish; it is now possible to `deployApp` almost any directory of content, and to `deployDoc` any single file. We'll try to ascertain whether the content needs special treatment (i.e. it's a Shiny or R Markdown asset); if not, we fall back on "static content" and just upload it as-is.

Add features for deploying static content
description:
This change adds support for deploying more content types from the rsconnect package. In particular:
1. The package is now able to deploy content to the RPubs service, via `rsconnect::rpubsUpload`. This function is a straightforward port of what was formerly an internal RStudio function, except that it now uses the HTTP transports provided by the rsconnect package, and writes deployment records which can be read by `rsconnect::deployments`. 
2. The package is now able to deploy static content to servers that support it. The static content mode is inferred when the set of files to be deployed includes no .Rmd files, no apparent Shiny layout, and at least one .html file. 
3. It is now possible to include custom metadata in the deployment record; the information is passed to `deployApp` and returned in `deployments`.

The new interface is backwards-compatible with the previous one.

title: Assume multiple Rmd docs are static unless >= 1 is Shiny (fixes #19)
Store deployment records for individual documents
description:
This change alters the way deployment records are stored when individual documents are deployed, with the goal of making deployments of individual documents feel like first-class operations rather than scoped deployments of their parent directories. 

Formerly, all records for any deployment made from a directory were stored in a subdirectory called `rsconnect`, which was further partitioned into folders for servers and username.

```
rsconnect
| 
+--servername
   |
   +--username 
      |
      +--appname1.dcf
      |
      +--appname2.dcf
```

After the change, there's a new folder beneath `rsconnect` that stores deployment records for individual documents; each document has its own `rsconnect/documents/docname.Rmd` folder. The structure of this folder mirrors that of the deployment records for the directory as a whole. (Note that it's relatively unlikely that the same directory will contain both directory-level and document-level deployments). 

```
rsconnect
| 
+--documents
|  |
|  +--mydocument.Rmd
|     |
|     +--servername
|        |
|        +--username 
|           |
|           +--appname1.dcf
|           |
|           +--appname2.dcf
|
+--servername
   |
   +--username 
      |
      +--appname3.dcf
      |
      +--appname4.dcf
```

Most of the functions that formerly took an `appDir` to specify a directory now take an `appPath`, which can refer either to a directory or an individual document. For instance, to show the logs for an individual document after deploying it:

```
rsconnect::showLogs("~/mydir/myfile.Rmd")
```

title: Emit primary R Markdown filename to manifest JSON (infer if unspecified)
description: This change emits a new parameter to the manifest JSON that identifies the primary R Markdown document being deployed. The parameter can be user-specified in `deployApp`, but can also be inferred from the contents being deployed.

title: Add features to deploy single documents and specific files
description:
This change adds two new features:
1. `deployApp` formerly deployed all content in the app directory, less a list of hard-coded exclusions. It now takes an optional argument called `appFiles`, which is a user-specified list of files to deploy that can be used in place of the auto-generated list.
2. A new function, `deployDoc`, extracts an R Markdown document's dependencies (using heuristics recently added to the `rmarkdown` package) and supplies them as input to `deployApp`. It can be used to deploy a single document and its supporting resources to ShinyApps or a local service.

Note that `deployDoc` is supplied mostly as a convenience for those who want to deploy documents directly at the console; it will not be invoked by the IDE. RStudio will include a GUI front end over `deployApp` that supports the interactive construction of `appFiles`.

title: don't include appmode in manifest for shinyapps
description: shinyapps.io does strong validation of deployment manifests so will fail if an extra field (appmode in this case) is included. This PR makes the accountInfo available to the manifest generation code and only includes appmode if we aren't running against shinyapps.io.

title: Refine absolute path lint mechanics
description:
Previously, we used a set of regular expressions applied on strings in documents indiscriminately to try and pull entries out that looked like absolute paths. This caused a lot of false positives, especially with URIs beginning with `/`, for example (as those can 'look like' absolute paths to files on the local filesystem).

This PR refines that behaviour by:
1. Extracting all (single and double quoted) strings in the document of at least 5 characters in length, and
2. Warning only if they 'look like' absolute paths, _and_ they exist on the local filesystem.

title: Show RStudio source markers for lint, if enabled

title: feature/migrate shinyapps
description:
This PR implements migration of the deployment records in the `shinyapps` directory to the `rsconnect` directory.

Prior to enumerating existing application deployments we check for the presence of a `shinyapps` directory. If it's there then we move it's contents into the `rsconnect/shinyapps.io` directory by reading in all of the DCF files, adding `server: shinyapps.io` to each record, then writing them into the appropriate spot within the `rsconnect` directory.

Note that this is a _move_ rather than _copy_ operation. This is because if we left the files in the shinyapps directory then:
1. We'd have to somehow _know_ which deployment record was current (i.e. whether we needed to migrate again, which one to actually use when there are two, etc.);
2. Users would be confused by the presence of two directories and might delete one of them incorrectly.

At the end of the migration if the `shinyapps` directory is completely empty (i.e. nothing other than deployment records were in there) we also remove it from the filesystem.

title: Migrate rsconnect deployment records from shinyapps.io to Connect Cloud
description:
Adds a way to migrate an app's local deployment record from shinyapps.io to Posit Connect Cloud, so that the next `deployApp()` call — including the RStudio IDE's Publish button — routes to the already-migrated Connect Cloud content instead of the original server. New functions added:

- **migrateDeployment(appPath, contentId, cloudAccount, name, account, server)** - resolves and validates the local source deployment record first, then calls the Connect Cloud API to confirm the target content exists, writes a new `.dcf` record, and removes the superseded source record
- **ensureConnectCloudAccount()** - an internal guard called at the start of `migrateDeployment()`. If no Connect Cloud account is registered, it offers a `cli_menu()` choice between the browser device-auth flow or pointing the user at `connectCloudClientCredentials()` for CI/non-interactive use.

Closes rstudio/lucid-server#5700.

### Manual Testing

- Registered a live shinyapps.io account and deployed a Shiny app to it.
- Deployed the same app to Connect Cloud to create a real migration target, then used forgetDeployment() to reset to shinyapps.io as the only active record (simulating the pre-migration state).
- Ran migrateDeployment() against the live shinyapps.io record with the real Connect Cloud content ID — succeeded, and deployments() afterward confirmed exactly one record remained, correctly pointing at connect.posit.cloud with the right appId, and the shinyapps.io record gone.

title: Reconstruct migration record from contentId when no local record exists
description:
Follow-up to #1353. Closes https://github.com/rstudio/lucid-server/issues/5706

For users whose local record is gone, the merged version had no recovery path - this closes that gap without requiring the shinyapps source bundle or `appId`. When no source record is found:

- The Connect Cloud record is reconstructed from `contentId` alone (which `getContent()` already verifies exists).
- The record `name` comes from `appName`, or is derived from the content's title via `generateAppName()` when `appName` is omitted - Connect Cloud content has no server-side name to reuse, only a title.
- The source-removal step is skipped (there is nothing to remove).

### Testing
1. Run `migrateToConnectCloud(appDir, contentId)` from a working directory where there is no deployment record.
2. It should create a Connect Cloud record from `contentId`.
3. `deployApp(appDir)` should send deployments to connect.posit.cloud.

title: Add Posit Connect Cloud support to applications() and collaborator management functions
description:
Adds Posit Connect Cloud (PCC) support to `applications()` and to the five collaborator-management functions (`addAuthorizedUser`, `removeAuthorizedUser`, `showUsers`, `showInvited`, `resendInvitation`), and soft-deprecates those five functions.

`applications()` previously aborted for PCC accounts; it now lists PCC content via a paginated content request and returns the same column shape as the other server types. The five collaborator functions gain PCC code paths for inviting, listing, and removing members and pending invitations. On PCC, these functions identify their target content by the local deployment record's content id rather than by application name — PCC content titles are neither unique nor stable, so name matching isn't a safe identity — and they error clearly when no deployment record is present for the given directory. A guard also keeps a record-less PCC deploy from adopting existing same-titled content instead of creating new content.

The five collaborator functions are soft-deprecated with `lifecycle::deprecate_warn()`, firing once per call on both shinyapps.io and PCC.

Notes for reviewers:

- The deprecation message wording is a placeholder and will be finalized before release; the `when` version is the current development version and should be bumped to the release version before CRAN submission.
- On PCC, `sendEmail = FALSE` is not honored (the platform always emails invitees) and `showInvited()`/`resendInvitation()` cannot surface an invitation link/code — the platform never returns one to the caller. Both are documented in the functions' notes and, for `sendEmail`, warned at runtime.
- `showUsers()` and `showInvited()` now build their data frames with atomic columns on all backends, so ids are returned as character and empty results are typed zero-row data frames (a visible change for existing shinyapps.io callers, noted in NEWS).
- The new PCC client methods are covered by request-level tests against mocked endpoints; they have not been exercised against a live PCC account.

title: Add contentId argument to collaborator management functions
description:
Adds an optional `contentId` argument to the five collaborator-management functions (`addAuthorizedUser`, `removeAuthorizedUser`, `showUsers`, `showInvited`, `resendInvitation`).

On Posit Connect Cloud, passing `contentId` targets the content directly, so a local deployment record is no longer required. `resolveContentTarget()` short-circuits to `list(id = contentId)` when an id is supplied, and rejects `contentId` on shinyapps.io. The id is shown in the content URL and returned by `applications()`, so the discovery-to-management workflow no longer depends on running from a project directory with an `rsconnect/` record.

Precedence: when `contentId` is supplied, `appDir` and `appName` are ignored.

### Notes for reviewers

- `contentId` is placed after `appName` in each signature, which shifts `account`/`server` by one position. These functions are near-always called by name, but if positional 4+ arg calls are a concern, `contentId` could move to the end instead.
- Supplying both `contentId` and `appName` is a quiet override (no warning). Happy to add a warning if preferred.
- `contentId` is PCC-only; on shinyapps.io it aborts with a clear message.
